answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may vote or claim scarce work, then slash that stake when an audit proves coordinated duplicate identities. One attacker can still create many accounts, but must lock real capital for each and risk losing it; splitting a stake across a glacier of aliases does not multiply influence. Audits that compare behavior across accounts can catch an echo of the same operator, while delayed withdrawals make a last-minute swarm costly even at the zenith of demand.
